name: Template Workshop
character: Acrylic templates laser-cut to the thousandth: rulers, nesting sets, and custom one-offs from a real machine shop.

sections.title: Quarter-inch seams argue less with a true edge

items.title: To the thousandth

sections.heading: The shop floor
sections.html: Half the building is a 1963 machine shop that used to make textile mill parts; the other half is a quilt room where the prototypes get sewn. If a template cannot survive a beginner's rotary cutter and an expert's stash? an expert's stash, it does not get etched, packed, or sold.

sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Rulers, nesting sets, and the specialty shapes that only exist because a quilt asked for them.

sections.heading: Shops and wholesale
sections.html: Quilt shops carry the line on net-thirty terms with a counter display that ships flat. Write through the contact page and the wholesale sheet comes back the same week, with the display and the first dozen sets priced to try.

sections.title: Tutorials
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: How to read the etched lines, cut with the grain? with confidence, and get the math right the first time.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.html: New to acrylic? Read the seam-allowance guide before the first cut: the etched lines are the stitching line, the solid edge is the cutting line, and everything else on the ruler is a bonus you will earn later.

sections.title: About {{guild_name}}
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: A machinist, a quilter, a marriage, and one argument about whether 0.015 of an inch matters. It does.

sections.html:
The shop ran three shifts making spindle parts until the mills closed. The quilter in the family inherited the laser along with the building, and the first template was a hexagon cut for her guild because the paper ones kept drifting. The guild ordered forty. The mill parts line never came back, and nobody here misses it.

Every design is sewn before it is sold, on the long arm in the quilt room, by the same hands that etch the lines. The tolerances are a family inheritance; the yardage charts are pure apology for every template that ever shipped without one.

items.quote: I sent a crayon sketch of an odd kite shape and got back a template better than the original block. The math sheet alone taught me something.
items.author: A scrappy quilter, Lowell

sections.title: Custom work
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: One-offs, small runs, and replacement pieces for templates the dog ate. Sketches are a fine starting point.

items.q: What can I send instead of a drawing?
items.a: A photograph of the block, a paper template taped to graph paper, or the worn original you want duplicated. The laser needs one clean dimension to start from, and we will find it together.

items.q: How small a run do you take?
items.a: One. A single template is a real order here; the setup is the work and the setup is already paid for.
Most customs cut within a week and ship polished and wrapped. December customs should start their conversation at Thanksgiving.

sections.heading: The machine shop annex
sections.html: The laser runs weekdays; the quilt room runs whenever the light is good. Write before you drive: the front door is the one with the hexagon etched in the glass, and the parking is on the mill yard side.
